description: Exposed under fz-k22.7 after Layers A/B/C cleared the capture-ABI crashes. A plain (non-closure) Term::Call/TailCall to a shared body passes only 4 args at ONE call site while every other call site to the same fn correctly passes 5. Direct call -> arity is a property of the callees compiled signature, NOT capture-ABI/target-identity resolution -- judged LIKELY SEPARATE from the k22 capture-ABI family. Precise repro: fixtures2/behavior/enum_predicate_search.fz via run/build; error at native_codegen verify stage; functions reduce_while_cont__clause_{0,1}; callee fn6/fn7 (colocated u0:224 / u0:857 in dumped IR); signature (i64,i64,i64,i64,i64)->i64 tail; call site supplies 4. May connect to the reduce_while_cont demand/materialization territory (near the closed fz-k22.8 clause-0 work). Blocks enum_predicate_search + enum_take_drop_split run/build.

comments.text:
SCOPE: this ticket covers BOTH run/build blockers now, same root (reduce_while_cont's shared body reached with INCONSISTENT physical arg/capture shapes across call sites):
- enum_predicate_search run/build: surfaces at the cranelift VERIFIER -- reduce_while_cont clause_0/clause_1 direct call passes 4 args to a 5-param tail-CC body (fn6/fn7).
- enum_take_drop_split run/build: surfaces at the fz-k22.7 Layer-C boundary ABI-agreement guard -- two resolutions to one shared target disagree on physical ABI (arg/capture/return reprs); the guard CORRECTLY hard-errors rather than silently picking one (would miscompile). Greening needs a real resolution: specialize the shared body per-ABI, or give it a uniform boxed ABI, OR fix the upstream cause that lets one body be called with two arg-vector shapes.
Both are the argument-shape-consistency problem for the shared reduce_while continuation, distinct from the capture-ABI conflation (which fz-k22.7 Layers 1/A/B/C resolved). Interp blocker is separate (fz-k22.9).

SPIKE (2026-07-09, branch wt/k22-10-reduce-arity @ 819ef0fc5 = telemetry only, kept for follow-up). NOT green: this is TWO distinct bugs, same family (coarse identity merges physically-incompatible resolutions of one shared body), different layers. Greening BOTH fixtures run/build needs BOTH fixed (fixing A immediately re-exposes B on both).

THIS TICKET = BUG A (callable-boundary layer, enum_take_drop_split CallableId(20) 2-vs-3-lane): a reducer closure literal (e.g. take_every's reducer FunctionId(191)) invoked through >1 Enumerable impl's reduce_while_cont (List grounds reducer.(head,acc) at boxed ValueRef, Range at raw RawInt) legitimately has multiple disagreeing-ABI resolutions on CallableFacts. callable_for_producer (transport.rs:3291-3422) classifies it direct-only (boundary_surface_demands empty -> boundary_ids=[]), so native fallback_callable_boundary (native.rs:3015-3140, strict-agreement check ~3086-3107 = fz-k22.7's guard) is the only path and correctly hard-errors.
FIX SHAPE (concrete, non-regressing): do NOT promote such producers to the first-class boundary-publish path -- that regresses 5 lib tests (multi-surface AGREEING-ABI producers are common/safe; forcing them through boundary-publish exposes a capture-lane accounting gap). Instead, in fallback_callable_boundary: GROUP resolutions by (arg_reprs, return_reprs, return_tuple_arity), mint ONE NativeCallableBoundary per group, and have materialize_transport_value's call site pick the group matching its OWN Clause/ExecutableKey origin context -- mirroring how settled_callable_boundary/select_inhabited_callable_boundary already tolerate multiple boundaries. The disagreement can only be resolved soundly at the NATIVE layer (physical reprs exist), not at transport from Tys.

BUG B split to a new ticket (direct-call 4-vs-5-arg). NON-DETERMINISM finding split to a new ticket. Telemetry FZ_K22_10_TRACE=1 env-gated eprintln in world.rs::intern_callable, transport.rs::callable_for_producer, TransportFactsBuilder::finish (on branch, inert).

HOLISTIC RE-SPIKE (2026-07-09/10, branch wt/k22-10-reduce-arity @ be54e0126). Deeper than the prior spike: found the earliest point of rot, empirically confirmed. Full report delivered to caller; summary here for persistence.

FIRST POINT OF ROT: src/compiler2/semantic.rs -- `CallSiteSummary::same_call_target` (line ~134-136: `left.callee == right.callee`, comparing only `SelectedCallee` i.e. bare FunctionId) is the join/coalesce key used by both `coalesce_targets` and `replace_targets_join_returns` to decide "is this the same call target." It has NO Ty/activation component at all. The companion `merge_callsite_activation` (line ~154) then decides which ActivationKey survives the merge, guarded only by `current.root == observed.root && current.function == observed.function` -- omitting `arrow` (the Ty component of ActivationKey that IS the per-specialization dispatch identity, per identity.rs). When both guards fire, the SECOND ActivationKey's distinct `arrow` Ty is silently discarded; exactly one arbitrary activation survives per callsite.

Telemetry proof: added two FZ_K22_10_TRACE eprintln probes (one per site above). Ran against a minimal 8-line repro (take_every AND drop_every, each over List AND Range) and observed 14 "DISCARDING divergent arrow" events, including one on a FunctionId matching the reduce_while_cont family, e.g. `kept=ActivationKey{function: FunctionId(182), arrow: Ty(258)} discarded=ActivationKey{function: FunctionId(182), arrow: Ty(209)}`.

ISOLATION MATRIX (empirical, new finding beyond the prior spike): take_every alone (List+Range) = GREEN. drop_every alone (List+Range) = GREEN. take_every AND drop_every together (List+Range) = CRASHES with the exact Facet-B shape (4 args to 5-param callee), in an 8-line fixture -- confirms the coalescing requires 2+ DISTINCT producer/accumulator specializations sharing one shared-body FunctionId, not merely List-vs-Range on one producer. This event fires even in some GREEN runs too (e.g. exp_take_multi: 9 occurrences, still green) -- so the coalescing itself is routine/load-bearing and only unsafe when the discarded activation's TRUE executable disagrees in physical arity/shape from the survivor's. There is NO ABI-agreement guard on this direct-call path analogous to fz-k22.7's boundary guard -- so a mismatch is either caught late as a raw cranelift verifier crash (what we see) or, in the worse case, could silently miscompile if the two arities coincide but shapes differ (never proven safe).

CONCLUSION: Facet A (enum_take_drop_split, CallableFacts 2-vs-3-lane) and Facet B (enum_predicate_search / fz-k22.12, 4-vs-5-arg) are the SAME defect family ("coarse identity merges physically-incompatible resolutions of one shared body") reproduced via TWO DIFFERENT subsystems: Facet A trips transport.rs's `callable_for_producer` (which correctly enumerates multiple resolutions and is caught by fz-k22.7's ABI-agreement guard -- working as designed). Facet B (and my new minimal repro) trips this semantic.rs CallSiteSummary coalescing instead, which has no equivalent guard.

FIX SHAPE: key `same_call_target` (and the merge it feeds) by the full demanded ActivationKey (root, function, arrow), not bare FunctionId -- mirroring fz-k22.7's "identity belongs to the target, not the reference" principle, now applied to direct-call target selection. Where two demanded ActivationKeys for one FunctionId truly diverge, the callsite must carry BOTH targets forward (a real dispatch-shaped CallEdge, or an explicit boundary/escape), analogous to how CallableFacts already tolerates multi-resolution producers -- not silently keep one. A pre-codegen fatal length-check on the args/input_bindings zip in native.rs (native_direct_call_target_and_args, ~line 1442) remains warranted regardless as a last-resort guard (fz-k22.12), but is NOT sufficient by itself since the true fix must prevent the wrong activation from being selected in the first place, not merely fatal cleanly when it is.

Telemetry left in place (inert without FZ_K22_10_TRACE=1): world.rs::intern_callable, transport.rs::callable_for_producer/finish (prior spike) + semantic.rs::coalesce_targets/merge_callsite_activation (this spike). cargo test --lib: 1301/1 (the 1 failure -- compiler2_multi_target_closure_arg_floor_clears_the_shared_reducer_demand_crash -- is pre-existing at HEAD~1, unrelated, itself a pinned-open k22-family gap).

PULL-LENS UNIFICATION (2026-07-10): fz-k22.10 (root) + fz-k22.12 (Facet B 4-vs-5-arg) + fz-k22.13 (non-determinism) are ONE bug. The coalescing keeps one ARBITRARY activation among divergent arrows -- 'arbitrary' violates the north-star 'graph is deterministic given the root': the survivor is chosen by observation/HashMap order, which IS the fz-k22.13 non-determinism (3 failure messages across runs). same_call_target/coalesce_targets is a PASS-shaped mechanism (extreme-suspicion per the pull principle): it imposes a single-target assumption and collapses a genuinely-DISPATCHED callsite (2 demanded callee activations) into one. Pull-correct behavior: a callsite's target set = exactly what demand reaches; 2 activations => a real CallEdge::Dispatch carried faithfully, never an arbitrary merge-to-one. Fix = key same_call_target + merge_callsite_activation by the full ActivationKey (root, function, arrow); where two demanded ActivationKeys for one FunctionId diverge, carry BOTH forward as dispatch/boundary, never discard. Over-specialization is bounded by construction: convergence-class collapse (widen_for_recursive_spec_key) already folds arrows that should be one identity BEFORE this point, so surviving-distinct arrows are genuinely distinct. Verify the fix ALSO makes the coalescing deterministic (closes fz-k22.13) and greens both fixtures run/build. fz-k22.12's native.rs length-check stays as a last-resort fatal guard only.

FIX-SHAPE CORRECTED (spike 3, 2026-07-10, reverted clean at be54e0126). The prescribed 'key by full ActivationKey -> route divergent through CallEdge::Dispatch' fix is WRONG on two independent grounds:
1. EMPIRICAL: on enum_predicate_search the divergent-arrow pairs (e.g. FunctionId(174) arrows Ty(300) vs Ty(327)) have BYTE-IDENTICAL surface_inputs [Ty(21),Ty(85)] -- the divergence lives only in the finer arrow (convergence-collapse/recursion mask, canonical_activation_key world.rs:2682). CallEdge::Dispatch keys on surface_inputs.first(), so two rows with identical precondition can't branch -> either second-arm-unreachable (MISCOMPILE) or Indirect boxing destroys return_call tail-call. Implemented anyway -> both fixtures still crash (same arity mismatch, different index).
2. INVARIANT: the fix regresses 2 deliberately-authored tests over fixtures2/behavior/opaque_fn_value_join.fz (add_a/add_b structurally identical, joined into one callable for Enum.reduce): compiler2_semantic_callsite_joins_duplicate_function_targets_before_artifact + compiler2_transport_plan_keeps_joined_enum_reduce_reducer_callable_shaped. Their explicit intent: callsite summaries MUST JOIN repeated observations of one callee INSTEAD OF leaving artifact to dispatch by activation-key differences -- the literal opposite of the prescribed fix.

CORRECTED PULL-CORRECT FIX: merge_callsite_activation/merge_target_activation ARE the arbitrary keep-first-seen push/pass smell (confirmed). The right replacement is NOT keep-one and NOT let-both-survive: RECOMPUTE the surviving activation as a deterministic function of the JOINED, WIDENED surface_inputs via World::canonical_activation_key (the sole mint, identity.rs:98) -- a real deterministic join. BLOCKER: that recompute needs &mut World (convergence-collapse mask), but the merge is at CallSiteMap::define which only has &mut Types. Threading World into define + all callers is an ARCHITECTURE change, not spike-sized.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY (falsifiable): for opaque_fn_value_join (different inputs -> different arrows) recompute is clearly correct. For enum_predicate_search (IDENTICAL inputs -> different arrows) recompute-from-inputs collapses both to one deterministic arrow -- fixes it ONLY IF that arrow matches the callee's true ABI. If not, ABI-loss is further upstream in the recursive self-call's own ABI selection, independent of this callsite-summary struct. NEXT STEP: thread World into the merge, recompute, rerun both fixtures -> green confirms; still-crash means look upstream at recursive self-call ABI selection.

OPTION B RESULT (spike 4, 2026-07-10, branch wt/k22-10-reduce-arity @ 5c192ae09, DO NOT LAND as-is -- regresses 6 fixtures). The falsifiable test is RESOLVED: the deterministic recompute (thread coalesce up to World::define_callsite_summary where canonical_activation_key lives; CallSiteMap::define becomes a pure store; recursive divergent activations re-derived via canonical_activation_key on the widened join of the activations' .inputs()) is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. Both enum_predicate_search + enum_take_drop_split stay red with the IDENTICAL 'got 4, expected 5' signature -- and the pre-fix baseline shows the same shape -> THE ABI-LOSS IS UPSTREAM of CallSiteSummary, in the recursive self-call's OWN ABI selection. That upstream locus is now the REAL root of this ticket's 4-vs-5 crash.

What the recompute DID establish: the arbitrary keep-first-seen merge is genuinely gone for the RECURSIVE case (correct-by-construction, order-independent, unit-tested). Guardrail opaque_fn_value_join tests stay green. But the NON-recursive divergent case is a real architectural gap (see new ticket) and the committed least-Ty-id compromise regresses 6 fixtures (bsx_nested_eq, enum_map_family::interp, fz_f98_range_map_converges x3), so this commit is NOT landable. fz-k22.13 non-determinism is ALSO upstream (Ty-interning/scheduling) -- present identically in baseline, NOT the coalescing pick.

NEXT: investigate the recursive self-call ABI selection (where reduce_while_cont's own call passes 4 for a 5-param). The clean recompute + architecture cleanup can be revived alongside the non-recursive machinery.
